title: Burned one loaf, two others were fine. Moves a lot while kneading. Not as good as my older maker
text:
Burned one loaf, two others were fine. Moves a lot while kneading. Not as good as my older maker. I have a very inexpensive ( under forty dollars) Sunbeam bread maker that's happily produced good bread a couple of times a week for almost four years. It's larger than this Hamilton Beach machine and significantly heavier. This machine is prettier with it's stainless and black color - it matches my big appliances.

As for the actual bread making, I think this one has it's good points, but in the end, my old machine is better overall. This one does have a handy little tool for removing the paddle from the fresh loaf and the included flour cup and tea/table spoon.

I made a simple, buttermilk sandwich loaf first and bacon cheddar bread the second time. Both are our standard, go-to breads here and I typically make one of each every week. The buttermilk bread on the light crust setting came out dense, moist and a little chewy as it should. The basic cycle here is actually about 14 minutes longer than with my old Sunbeam maker. The bacon cheddar bread on a medium crust setting didn't fare so well. Halfway through the bake cycle, smoke billowed out of the lid and I had to unplug the entire thing - the uncooked, slightly blackened bread went in the trash. There was nothing in the bottom of the machine to cause the burn, so I don't know what the problem was. I have since made another buttermilk bread without a repeat of the smoke.

My real issue with this bread maker is that it bounces, wobbles and walks all over the counters as it mixes and kneads the dough. This could present a serious safety problem if you have limited counter space or set it too close to the edge. It moves about 8 inches every time I use it. My old machine literally has never bounced or shifted one iota. So, because of the bounce and the smoke issue, I will only use this again as an emergency back up to my older bread maker.

description: The Hamilton Beach artisan dough & bread maker lets you create everything from a loaf of basic white to fresh focaccia dough, without even having to roll up your sleeves to mix and knead. Just add ingredients, select the cycle, and press start. Designed with nutrition in mind, this bread maker features 14 programmed settings including gluten-free and whole-grain so you can use a variety of flours.
